title: Platform systems & services: playbook, dashboards, runbooks, roadmap, retrospective (Q3 2026) - Addendum
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Purpose and scope

This addendum supplements the Platform Systems & Services playbook (Q3 2026) with clarifications, new runbook links, updated alert thresholds based on Aug 2026 telemetry, and a short post-game-day summary (Sep 2026). Intended audience: platform engineers, SREs, on-call leads, and platform product managers.

Key clarifications

- Alert owner semantics: the page-level owner remains eng-platform, but each alert rule must include an explicit primary and secondary owner (team/email) in the alert annotation.
- Dashboard retention: all primary dashboards must retain 30 days of 1s resolution metrics and 13 months of 1m resolution metrics.
- Paging windows: P1/P0 pages are suppressed between 02:00 and 04:00 PT for non-customer impacting maintenance when a maintenance window is declared; otherwise pages proceed.

Updated alert thresholds (effective 2026-08-31)

- API request error rate: updated to P1 when 5m avg > 4% (previously 5%) for high-traffic routes (ingress > 100 rps).
- P99 generation latency: updated to P1 when > 1800ms for hosted models with 500ms SLOs (previously 2000ms).
- KV cache hit rate: P2 when < 65% for 10m (previously 60%).
- GPU memory pressure: P1 when > 88% (previously 90%).

New runbooks and links

- rollout-validation (owner: eng-serving-runtime): pre-deploy checklist and automated compatibility gate tests. Link: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/rollout-validation
- autoscale-canary (owner: eng-infra): steps to create a canary release for HPA/cluster-autoscaler changes, including test traffic profile and metrics to watch. Link: /confluence/eng-infra/autoscale-canary
- payload-schema-reject (owner: eng-developer-experience): how to triage rejected payloads surfaced by CI or the schema registry. Link: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/payload-schema-reject

Game day (2026-09-01): summary and findings

- Scenario executed: simultaneous model rollback + delayed scale-up under synthetic traffic (peak 1.5x normal).
- Observations:
  - Rollback automation executed successfully in 92% of canaries; two canaries required manual intervention due to missing artifact metadata.
  - Autoscale canary revealed an HPA metric mismatch in one cluster (chart templating bug) that would have impacted production in the event of a surge.
  - Alert routing to the on-call runbook link succeeded for 100% of triggered alerts; average time to acknowledge was 3m 20s.

Game day action items (owners and ETA)

1) Enforce artifact metadata schema (owner: eng-serving-runtime) 
 ETA: 2026-09-15. Add CI step to reject artifacts missing kernel/quantization metadata.
2) Chart templating tests (owner: eng-infra) 
 ETA: 2026-09-10. Add templating unit tests and a presubmit that renders charts against a matrix of cluster configs.
3) Improve runbook discoverability (owner: eng-platform) 
 ETA: 2026-09-20. Surface runbook links directly in Grafana/Loki alert annotations and in pager messages.

Action status tracking

- All game day items have corresponding issues in the eng-platform Jira board under epic EP-PLT-2026-GAMEDAY. Please reference that epic for status and owners.

Operations notes and best practices

- When creating or changing alerts, include the following annotations: summary, impact, primary_owner, secondary_owner, runbook_link, runbook_version, runbook_last_tested.
- Tag dashboards with component and SLO tags to allow automatic inclusion in the Platform Overview rollup. Example labels: component=serving-runtime, slo=latency-model-gen.
- Quarterly reviews: dashboard owners must publish a short review note in the dashboard description including the last review date and reviewer initials.

Changelog (addendum)

- 2026-08-31: adjusted alert thresholds to reflect telemetry trends (Ava Martinez)
- 2026-09-02: published addendum with game day summary and new runbook links (Ava Martinez)
